Precimax Industries - Q3 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Precimax Industries Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Precimax Industries' results for the Q3 FY2024. Joining me on today's call are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Alex Rivera, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Precimax Industries' performance for the Q3 FY2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. First, our revenue showed strong growth across geographic regions, with the Americas leading the charge at 18% year-over-year expansion. Second, we're guiding operating margins higher for the full year, targeting 15.2% to 16.2% amid pricing discipline and productivity gains. Third, organic revenue growth hit 8%, complemented by inorganic boosts from recent acquisitions. Fourth, supply chain constraints have eased notably, with on-time delivery rates reaching 92%. Fifth, order intake remains robust, with expectations for $1.3 to $1.4 billion in Q4 and healthy backlog conversion. Sixth, operating margins expanded across segments, particularly in automation and robotics. And seventh, inventory levels are well-managed, with days outstanding improving to 82 amid smart strategies.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, John. Turning to our financial performance, Precimax Industries reported $1.25 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 14% increase year-over-year and 8% on an organic basis, excluding the impact of our recent acquisition of Precision Robotics Solutions. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, driven by robust demand for our core offerings in CNC machining centers, collaborative robots, or cobots, and IoT-enabled automation systems. Gross margin was 28.5%, driven by localized supply chains, pricing power, and Factory 4.0 productivity. Operating expenses were $185 million, resulting in an operating income of $180 million. Our net income for the quarter was $125 million, or $1.45 per share.

Good afternoon, everyone—let me now dive into our revenue performance by geographic region, which underscores the resilience of our diversified portfolio in the industrial equipment sector amid ongoing macroeconomic headwinds like persistent inflation, supply chain normalization, and geopolitical tensions. Our geographic mix remains balanced: Americas at 47% of total revenue, EMEA at 28%, APAC at 20%, and Rest of World at 5%. Book-to-bill ratio stood at 1.25x overall, reflecting strong order intake across all regions, with a $2.8 billion backlog providing excellent visibility into FY2025.

In the Americas, which accounted for 47% of revenue or $587 million, we saw 18% year-over-year growth and 5% sequentially. This region continues to be our growth engine, fueled by U.S. manufacturing reshoring and the capex resurgence in key end-markets like semiconductors, aerospace, and automotive. Revenue here benefited from a 25% surge in orders for our next-gen FlexArm cobots, which integrate AI-driven predictive maintenance—similar to advancements we've seen from peers like Rockwell Automation in their FactoryTalk platform. U.S. sales alone grew 22%, supported by the CHIPS Act and IRA-driven investments; for instance, we've secured multi-year supply agreements with fabs from Intel and TSMC's Arizona expansion, totaling over $150 million in booked orders. Canada contributed modestly with strength in oil & gas automation, up 12% on LNG project ramps. Margins here expanded 220 basis points to 28.5%, thanks to localized supply chains reducing ocean freight costs by 15%. Looking ahead, we expect continued tailwinds from infrastructure spending under the IIJA, positioning Americas for low-teens growth in Q4.

EMEA represented 28% of revenue, or $350 million, up 9% year-over-year and 3% sequentially. Performance was solid but tempered by energy volatility and softening German auto demand. Revenue growth was led by the UK and France, up 15% combined, driven by adoption of our EnergyWise series—electrified machining centers compliant with the EU Green Deal's Scope 3 emissions targets. We've seen particular traction in renewables, with wind turbine OEMs like Vestas ordering $80 million in high-precision gear hobbing equipment. Conversely, Central Europe faced headwinds from destocking at automotive tier-1s amid EV transition delays; Volkswagen Group's capex pause hit us for about 3 points of growth. Middle East exposure grew 20% via Saudi Aramco's downstream automation upgrades, leveraging our explosion-proof robotics akin to Fanuc's offerings. Regional margins held steady at 26%, bolstered by our Dusseldorf manufacturing facility's 95% on-time delivery rate. Strategically, we're accelerating localization with a new €50 million cobot assembly line in Poland to mitigate tariff risks and tap into the NextGenerationEU funds—expecting EMEA to accelerate to mid-teens growth as auto cycles recover in H1 2025.

APAC contributed 20% of revenue, or $250 million, flat year-over-year and down 2% sequentially. This region reflected mixed signals: strength in India and Southeast Asia offset weakness in China. China revenue declined 8% due to ongoing real estate overhang and factory utilization rates hovering at 75%—similar pressures impacting peers like ABB in their Q3 results. However, our semiconductor equipment sales there grew 10%, anchored by deals with SMIC and CXMT for 5nm node wafer fab automation. India exploded +35%, driven by 'Make in India' initiatives; we've shipped over 200 units of our TitanPro CNC mills to Foxconn's iPhone lines in Tamil Nadu, contributing $45 million. ASEAN markets like Vietnam and Thailand added 18% growth on electronics reshoring from apparel. Margins compressed slightly to 24.5% from FX headwinds and component shortages in rare earths for servo motors. Our strategic pivot—doubling R&D investment in edge-computing PLCs for smart factories—positions us well; we're targeting 15%+ APAC growth in FY2025 as China's stimulus kicks in and India's capex cycle matures.

Rest of World made up 5% of revenue, or $63 million, up 22% year-over-year and 7% sequentially. Latin America and Africa punched above their weight, with Brazil's mining sector booming on Vale and CSN orders for our heavy-duty drill rigs (+30%), and South Africa's platinum ramps. This segment's agility highlights our playbook for emerging markets: modular, scalable equipment with remote diagnostics to minimize downtime in low-connectivity environments.

In summary on revenue, our regional performance validates our 'glocal' strategy—global scale with localized execution—investing $120 million this year in regional tech hubs for Industry 4.0 integration, from 5G-enabled MES systems to carbon-neutral machining. While APAC navigates cyclicality, our exposure to secular trends like automation (60% of orders) and electrification (up 40% YoY) de-risks the portfolio. We maintain our FY2024 revenue guidance of $4.9-5.0 billion, with Q4 weighted toward Americas and EMEA.

Full-year 2023 consolidated revenue reached levels that set a strong foundation, but zooming into this quarter's growth, organic revenue growth—which excludes the impact of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange—was 7.2% for the full year to date and accelerated to 9.5% in Q3. That's ahead of our initial guidance and meaningfully outperforms the broader industrial equipment peer set. In our core General Industrial segment, including CNC machining centers, precision stamping presses, and automation systems, we delivered 8.1% organic growth, fueled by a 12% volume uptick in aftermarket parts and services. Pricing discipline added another 2.5 points, enabled by our leadership in high-precision, domestically produced components that benefit from the CHIPS Act subsidies and nearshoring trends. Book-to-bill in this segment ended the quarter at 1.25x, with backlog providing strong visibility.

Aerospace & Defense saw 6.8% organic growth, driven by sustained demand for our aerostructure tooling and composite layup systems, with OEM pull-through from Boeing and Airbus ramp-ups offsetting some commercial aviation softness. We also benefited from a 15% surge in defense-related orders for hypersonic test rigs and missile assembly automation. Regionally, North America contributed 65% of this growth. Our Energy & Infrastructure segment rounded out at 6.1% organic, with wind turbine blade molding equipment and LNG compressor skids leading, and orders for EV battery gigafactory conveyance systems jumping 25%. Our organic momentum ties directly to strategic initiatives like the rollout of our 'DynSmart 4.0' platform—an IoT-enabled suite of predictive maintenance sensors and AI-optimized controls integrated into our hydraulic presses and robotic welders. Adoption hit 40% of our installed base, driving recurring software revenue growth and improving customer uptime by 18%.

Shifting to inorganic contributions: Acquisitions accounted for 11.8% of our year-to-date revenue growth, pushing total growth into double digits. We closed the $320 million purchase of TechForge Robotics, adding revenue from their collaborative robot arms for automotive weld cells—a perfect tuck-in with immediate 15% EBITDA margins and $25 million in identified synergies. Then, Precision Aero Components for $180 million bolstered our A&D fastener insertion systems. Combined, these contributed meaningfully to top line, with cross-selling already yielding a 20% pipeline lift. This reflects our disciplined M&A playbook: bolt-on deals under 2x EV/EBITDA multiples, focused on adjacencies in high-growth verticals like electrification and autonomy. For FY2024, we guide organic revenue growth of 8-10%, with total growth of 12-15%.

As we wrap up thoughts on margins from Q2, where operating margins expanded 220 basis points year-over-year to 16.2%—driven by our disciplined pricing strategy and the initial benefits from our Factory 4.0 digital transformation initiatives—let me provide our forward guidance on operating margins. For Q4, we are guiding for operating margins in the range of 14.0% to 15.0%. This reflects a sequential moderation, primarily due to near-term headwinds in our cost structure, but underpinned by continued strength in our core end-markets.

On the cost side, we continue to navigate elevated input costs, with structural steel prices up approximately 8% year-to-date—mirroring trends seen across peers like Caterpillar and Nucor—and aluminum alloys rising 5-6% amid lingering supply constraints from bauxite disruptions in Guinea. Labor costs remain a pressure point, with wage inflation averaging 4.2% in our U.S. and European facilities, exacerbated by skilled machinist shortages. Ocean freight rates from our Asian suppliers have ticked up 10% quarter-over-quarter due to Red Sea rerouting, though this is largely transitory as we accelerate our nearshoring strategy.

Offsetting these, our pricing power remains robust, with Q4 pass-through expected at 70-80% of incremental costs, building on the 5.2% average price realization we achieved across our CNC lathes, multi-axis mills, and robotic welding systems. We're seeing particular strength in aftermarket services, where margins exceed 25%, fueled by uptime demand for our PrecisionGuard predictive maintenance software—tailored for heavy fab shops. Productivity levers are firing on all cylinders. Our Factory 4.0 rollout—now live in 60% of our global footprint, including our new Querétaro, Mexico plant—is delivering 12-15% throughput gains via digital twins and AI-optimized CAM programming, directly adding 100 basis points to Q4 margins. We've also locked in multi-year offtake agreements for rare earth magnets, insulating 40% of our EV drivetrain component line from China export volatility.

Regionally, Americas exposure supports margin stability, with U.S. capex rebounding in semiconductors and aerospace. Europe faces softer auto OEM orders but benefits from EU Green Deal subsidies for hydrogen electrolyzer tooling. APAC sees some compression from China's property sector slowdown, though Vietnam and India offsets are gaining traction.

For the full year 2024, we now guide operating margins to 15.2% to 16.2%, a 50 basis point increase at the midpoint from our prior outlook. This assumes Q4 acceleration as supply chains normalize. Key drivers include volume leverage from mid-single-digit organic growth, led by share gains in North American battery gigafactory equipment; mix shift to higher-margin electromechanical products rising to 35% of sales, including our new ServoMax II series for EV inverter assembly; capex efficiency from our $450 million FY24 plan focused on vertical integration of additive manufacturing; and SG&A discipline through zero-based budgeting and our ProcureAI platform, which has yielded $25 million in procurement savings YTD.

Strategically, we're positioning Precimax at the intersection of reshoring, electrification, and automation megatrends. U.S. CHIPS Act and IRA tailwinds are accelerating domestic fab and clean energy capex—our order book for wafer fab etchers is up 40% YoY. We're mitigating China risk by shifting 25% of electronics sourcing to Mexico and Thailand by year-end. Sustainability-wise, our Scope 1&2 emissions are down 18% via electrified factories, opening doors to ESG-linked financing.

This guidance incorporates our standard assumptions around FX, no material M&A, and stable tax rates at 24.5%. Risks include prolonged commodity spikes or a sharper China industrial slowdown, but our $1.2 billion cash position and 2.8x net debt-to-EBITDA provide ample dry powder.

Now, on supply chain constraints and component availability—a topic top-of-mind given the sector's volatility—I'm pleased to report meaningful progress. In Q3, our on-time-in-full delivery rate climbed to 92%, up from 78% in Q2. This supported our record revenue, with backlog at $3.8 billion. Semiconductor lead times for our PLC controllers and vision systems have normalized to 18-22 weeks, with 120% of Q4 needs secured and average chip costs down 12%. Power semiconductors like SiC MOSFETs remain elevated, up 25% YoY due to EV spillover.

On metals, hot-rolled coil steel stabilized at $650 per ton in North America, but aluminum rose 8% QoQ. Overall input cost inflation moderated to 4.2% YoY, holding gross margins at 28.5%. In Asia-Pacific, our largest sourcing hub, constraints are easing fastest—Taiwan's wafer production reduced allocation risks. We've diversified, shifting 20% of electronics assembly to Vietnam. Europe remains challenged by nickel spikes from Ukraine conflict, but we're accelerating nearshoring with a $150 million plant in Monterrey, Mexico. North America benefits from domestic steel covering 60% of needs.

Strategically, our Supply Chain Fortress program includes dual-sourcing—no single supplier exceeds 15% of critical BOM; digital forecasting improving accuracy to 95%; vertical integration like in-house SMT for PCBs; and hedging 70% of FY24 steel and aluminum. These moves have shielded EBITDA margins at 14.2%. For Q4, we expect OTIF to hit 95%, with risks from port strikes or Red Sea issues, but our China+1 strategy positions us well.

Order intake was robust at $1.25 billion in Q3, up 18% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, led by Discrete Automation and Robotics at $525 million. We expect Q4 intake between $1.3 billion and $1.4 billion, implying full-year guidance of $5.0 to $5.2 billion—a 15-20% increase. Book-to-bill at 1.25x signals demand strength. Backlog ended at a record $4.8 billion, up 22% YoY, representing 10 months of visibility—55% Discrete Automation, 30% Process Industries, 15% Energy Transition. Q3 conversion was 28%, up from 24% last year, thanks to supply chain resilience and our SmartForge digital twin platform reducing lead time variability by 35%. We anticipate Q4 at 27-29%. Americas drove 52% of intake, EMEA 28%, APAC 20%. Initiatives like $250 million CapEx for additive manufacturing and predictive maintenance SaaS will sustain these metrics.

Drilling into operating margin performance by segment, consolidated margins expanded 150 basis points to 14.5%, driven by pricing, mix shifts, and productivity. Automation & Robotics (32% of revenue, $1.2 billion) hit 18.2%, up 220 bps on 12% growth, with pricing, SaaS mix, and Lean Sigma savings. Heavy Earthmoving & Mining (28%, $1.05 billion) held at 13.8%, up 90 bps on mining backlog. Power Systems & Turbines (22%, $825 million) at 12.4%, flat revenue but SG&A leverage. Aerospace & Defense (18%, $675 million) jumped 310 bps to 16.7% on ramp-ups and digital twins. North America delivered 16.5% margins, guiding Q4 consolidated to 15-15.5%.

Finally, on inventory levels, total stood at $1.27 billion, up 2.4% sequentially but down 8.7% YoY, with DIO at 82 days versus industry 95. Finished goods down 12% YoY. North America at 75 DIO, EMEA 88, APAC 72. Strategies include AI demand sensing reducing errors 37%; VMI covering 22% of raw materials; RFID traceability; and modular platforms with 40% part commonality. We've localized 35% of electronics supply chain, targeting DIO sub-75 by FY25. Q4 should flatten as bookings accelerate.

We are committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and generating consistent cash flow.

Now, I will hand over to Lisa Patel, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our supply chain, improving manufacturing efficiency, and enhancing customer service—building directly on the supply chain progress Michael outlined, with OTIF at 92% and inventory turns at 5.2x. We are leveraging data analytics to identify areas for improvement and drive operational excellence, including our Factory 4.0 rollout across 60% of facilities for 12-15% throughput gains. We are also investing in employee training and development to build a highly skilled workforce, particularly in AI and digital twins for backlog conversion.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Alex Rivera, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Alex Rivera (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things, powering our DynSmart 4.0 platform and PrecisionGuard software now at 40% adoption. We are developing solutions to improve predictive maintenance and optimize our customer's operations, like FlexArm cobots and ServoMax II for EV assembly. Our new TitanPro CNC mill is exceeding expectations, with 35% growth in India shipments contributing $45 million and overall impact lifting automation segment margins to 18.2%.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the trends you are seeing in automation spending?

Dr. Alex Rivera (CTO):
Good morning, David. Automation spending remains a bright spot, with 60% of our orders tied to it. We're seeing robust demand for cobots and AI-integrated systems, up 25% in Americas from reshoring and CHIPS Act fabs. In APAC, despite China softness, India and ASEAN are exploding on Make in India and electronics reshoring. Our DynSmart 4.0 IoT platform is driving 3 points of recurring revenue, with uptime gains mirroring peers like Rockwell. Book-to-bill at 1.25x gives us confidence in continued mid-teens growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (JPMorgan):
What is your strategy for managing inflation and rising input costs?

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thanks, Emily. Inflation is moderating to 4.2% YoY, but we're proactive. Pricing realization at 5.2% passes through 70-80% of costs, with strength in 25%+ margin aftermarket. Factory 4.0 delivers 100 bps margin add via throughput gains. Hedging covers 70% of steel/aluminum, dual-sourcing limits supplier risk to 15%, and nearshoring to Mexico/Poland cuts freight 15%. Rare earth offtakes insulate EV lines. This supports our 15.2-16.2% full-year margin guide.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Robert Kim (Morgan Stanley):
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce your carbon footprint?

John Reynolds (CEO):
Absolutely, Robert. Sustainability is core, with Scope 1&2 emissions down 18% via electrified factories and EnergyWise series compliant with EU Green Deal. We've invested $120 million in carbon-neutral machining and regional hubs. Electrification orders up 40% YoY, positioning us for ESG financing advantages. Our glocal strategy de-risks while capturing green capex like wind OEMs and IRA incentives.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

John Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Precimax Industries. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
